abstract: Rohrbach's conjecture holds for finite groups. In fact, there is an absolute constant $C$ such that, for every finite group $G$, every positive integer $h$, and all nonnegative real numbers $\alpha_1,\ldots,\alpha_h$ with $\alpha_1+\cdots+\alpha_h=1$, there are subsets $A_1,\ldots,A_h\subseteq G$ satisfying \[ G=A_1\cdots A_h, \qquad |A_1|\leq |G|^{\alpha_1}, \qquad |A_i|\leq C|G|^{\alpha_i}\quad(2\leq i\leq h). \] Consequently, for every $h$ there is a constant $c_h$ such that every finite group $G$ has a subset $A$ with \[ A^h=G\qquad\text{and}\qquad |A|\leq c_h|G|^{1/h}. \]
hook: Every finite group can be covered by h products of small subsets, proving Rohrbach's conjecture.
summary: For any finite group and any h, there is a subset A of size at most a constant times the h-th root of the group's size whose h-fold product is the whole group. The result is stronger, allowing uneven subset sizes. It is a new preprint on a long-open problem, so expert verification is still pending.
title: Rohrbach's Conjecture for Finite Groups
